Bug_Title: The signature of "finalize()" should match that of "Object.finalize()"
Bug_Details:
Object.finalize() is called by the Garbage Collector at some point after the object becomes unreferenced.
In general, overloading Object.finalize() is a bad idea because:
The overload may not be called by the Garbage Collector. Users are not expected to call Object.finalize() and will get confused.
The overload may not be called by the Garbage Collector.
Users are not expected to call Object.finalize() and will get confused.
But beyond that it’s a terrible idea to name a method "finalize" if it doesn’t actually override Object.finalize() .
Noncompliant code example
public int finalize(int someParameter) {        // Noncompliant
  /* ... */
}
Compliant solution
public int someBetterName(int someParameter) {  // Compliant
  /* ... */
}
Bug_Explanation: The non-compliant finalize method has a different signature than Object.finalize.
Bug_Trigger_Explanation: The test results do not demonstrate the bug being triggered. The test case does not call the buggy method `finalize` directly, but instead calls `showBug`, which in turn calls `finalize` with a parameter. However, the `finalize` method in the test case is not the same as the one in the original code, and it does not have the same signature as `Object.finalize()`, so the bug is not triggered.
